distribution_shape.reason: Every finite value is identical, so the column has no spread and skewness is undefined.

measure.name: Adjusted Fisher-Pearson skewness coefficient (G1)
measure.calculation: G1 = g1 * sqrt(n * (n - 1)) / (n - 2), where g1 = m3 / m2^1.5 and m2, m3 are the second and third central moments of the finite values. Matches pandas Series.skew and scipy.stats.skew(bias=False).

thresholds.direction: negative is left-skewed (long tail of small values); positive is right-skewed (long tail of large values)

limitations: Approximate symmetry does not mean the values are normally distributed; flat or two-peaked distributions can also have skewness near zero.
Skewness is sensitive to a few extreme values; check the histogram and outlier counts alongside it.
Missing, NaN and infinite values are left out.
